$comment: Anti-aliasing and anisotropic filtering (ARCHITECTURE.md §6.10; owner: "Yes can we add anti aliasing… Should be a graphics setting"). `modes` are Settings → Graphics's Anti-aliasing choices: `samples` per pixel of the scene's multisampling (WebGPU allows only 1 or 4, so there is no 8× or 16× MSAA; dwell-client render/mod.rs `samples_for`), and `fxaa` a cheap post pass that smooths the edges multisampling leaves (render/fxaa.rs). The sample count is fixed when the renderer is made, so a change of `samples` applies on the next load; `fxaa` applies live. `anisotropy` is the block atlas's anisotropic filtering, its sampler's maxAnisotropy (1 off; WebGPU allows up to 16), applied live: far ground at a grazing angle stays sharp instead of blurring. A CPU adapter draws the cheapest of each (1 sample, no FXAA, anisotropy 1). Not part of a graphics preset.
hint: Smooths jagged edges. Browsers' WebGPU allows only 4× multisampling, so there is no 8× or 16×; FXAA adds a light post pass. A change of MSAA applies when the game next loads
anisotropyHint: Keeps far ground sharp at a grazing angle instead of blurring; higher costs a little GPU time
